q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution

Today is 2026-08-17. Q2 FY2027 earnings would typically be released around August-September 2026 (fiscal calendars often differ from calendar year). However, Q1 FY2027 was released on May 20, 2026, and the guidance was for Q2 FY2027, which means Q2 FY2027 earnings release would likely occur in late August or September 2026—essentially **immediately** (days to a few weeks away).

This is asking for a forward guidance already provided in the May 20, 2026 earnings release.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The research explicitly states that **NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%**.

This guidance was already announced on May 20, 2026. The question is asking what the forward guidance *will be* in the Q2 FY2027 earnings release—which has either already occurred or is about to occur within days.

The most straightforward interpretation is that we're forecasting whether NVIDIA's actual reported Q2 FY2027 guidance will match or deviate from this $91.0B ± 2% range. However, since this guidance was already provided and announced, the most likely outcome is that the guidance figure will remain at or very close to **$91.0 billion**, with the ±2% corridor being $89.18B–$92.82B.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Market deterioration or demand weakness** discovered between May and August that would force NVIDIA to lower guidance
- **Geopolitical or regulatory shocks** affecting China revenue (which is already excluded)
- **Competitive disruption** or customer inventory adjustments
- **Macro slowdown** affecting AI capex spending

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Better-than-expected demand** for AI accelerators forcing an upward revision
- **Surprise announcements** from major customers committing to larger orders
- **ASP increases** or favorable product mix shifts
- **Continued dominance** in data center with no meaningful competition emerging

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided:
- **Q1 FY2027 reported revenue: $81.6 billion** (reported)
- **Q2 FY2027 forward guidance: $91.0 billion ± 2%** (already announced on May 20, 2026)
- **Sequential growth implied: ~11.5%** from Q1 to Q2

NVIDIA has been on an extraordinary growth trajectory (85% YoY in Q1 FY2027, 92% in data center). An 11.5% sequential increase is conservative relative to recent growth rates but plausible given the scale of the business.

---

## Reasoning

The critical insight here is that this guidance was **already provided on May 20, 2026**. The question asks what the guidance "will be" in the Q2 FY2027 earnings release—but we already have this information from the current research block.

Unless there's a material deterioration or discovery between May 20 and the actual Q2 earnings release (late August/early September 2026), the guidance is most likely to remain at **$91.0 billion ± 2%**, giving us a range of **$89.18–$92.82 billion** at the ±2% level.

The midpoint of $91.0 billion is the single most likely outcome. Deviations would be unusual unless:
- Something catastrophic happened in the intervening months (low probability)
- NVIDIA decides to raise guidance due to exceptional demand (moderate probability)
- NVIDIA takes a conservative revision (low probability)

Given that the guidance was recently provided and NVIDIA typically doesn't make dramatic revisions within 2-3 months unless conditions change materially, I'll center my forecast on $91.0B with reasonable dispersion to account for potential upside (raised guidance) or downside (lowered guidance).

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for its second quarter of fiscal year 2027 (Q2 FY2027) revenue, released on May 20, 2026, is an expected **$91.0 billion**, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027/). This guidance does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html), [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027/). This figure is well above the average quarterly revenue estimate of $86.84 billion, according to LSEG [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html).

For Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported record revenue of $81.6 billion, an 85% increase from the previous year [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027/), driven by a 92% year-over-year increase in data center revenue [barchart.com](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3449043/what-to-expect-from-nvidia-s-q2-2027-earnings-report).
